audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart is blanket 'Skill' while content and packet both give Hwei levels 1-6 and Mel from first item. Full layer also never names a real Hwei ability — it tracks a fabricated 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)'.
audit.why: Real E is Subject: Torment (12s, the CC palette: Grim Visage / Gaze of the Abyss / Crushing Maw). Content whys are grounded: his layered Q poke out-ranges the volley pre-item; Mel's first-item clear plus Snare-into-Eclipse flips it.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced everywhere with Subject: Torment (E); full chart aligned to content win[] with grounded whys/ratings as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] names a fabricated 'EE (Stirring Sands)' as his escape and spikes[3] calls 'EQ (Fleeting Current)' a knock-up. Fleeting Current is the W-palette dash (WQ); Stirring Lights is the real WE; the E palette is CC, not mobility.
audit.why: Riot kit: W Subject: Serenity palette = Fleeting Current, Pool of Reflection, Stirring Lights; E palette = Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss, Crushing Maw.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] escape corrected to WQ Fleeting Current; spikes[3] dodge target corrected to the EW Gaze of the Abyss root; wants.you[1] corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: Missing interaction: Subject: Serenity's shield absorbing Mel's burst was never stated; no digits in cooldowns; two bleed bullets; the Rebuttal-bait dynamic lived only in content.
audit.why: W Serenity (18s) holds both his shield and his dash — forcing it before committing is the burst rule. Nearly all his paints are projectiles Rebuttal can return, which is exactly why he baits the glow with a cheap spell first.
audit.corrected: See edits: shield/dash rule in cooldowns bullet, bait truth in dontsFull[2].d, palette-cycle poke rule in dosFull[1].d.

notes: The full layer's tracked ability 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' does not exist — replaced with Subject: Torment (E) in every field it appeared (winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, cooldowns, feeding, dosFull[2].d, report[1]/[5]/[9]). Content's two-letter combo codes (QQ/QE/QW) are internally inconsistent and only the clear errors were fixed (Stirring Sands fabrication; Fleeting Current mislabeled EQ knock-up; 'pools with QW/EE'); the remaining codes in spikes[0]/early/mid are plausible but unverified against sub-ability order.
